criteria.name: Plain language
criteria.fiveMeans: No unexplained jargon; the listed jargon terms are replaced by plain words.

anchors.excerpt: 'The team lowered MTTR by tuning the SIEM correlation rules and triaging IOCs faster.'
anchors.why: Three unexplained terms in one sentence.

anchors.excerpt: 'The team got faster at fixing problems: they taught their alarm system to connect related warnings, so they could spot the real clues sooner.'
anchors.why: The same idea in everyday words, with nothing left to look up.

criteria.name: Rebuilt structure
criteria.fiveMeans: Organized for comprehension, not a mirror of the source outline.

anchors.excerpt: Sections: 'Slide 1 in simple words', 'Slide 2 in simple words', 'Slide 3 in simple words'.
anchors.why: Walks the source outline slide by slide.

anchors.excerpt: Sections: 'What the company is trying to do', 'The one number that matters', 'What could go wrong'.
anchors.why: Rebuilt around the questions a newcomer has.

anchors.excerpt: Source: 'The test found a lift that was not statistically significant.' ELI5: 'The test proved the new button works better.'
ELI5: 'The new button did a little better, but not by enough to be sure it was not luck, so the team will test longer.'
anchors.why: Simple and still true to the source.

criteria.name: Core idea
criteria.fiveMeans: A reader can state the main point after one read.

anchors.excerpt: Five equally weighted paragraphs about budgets, dates, owners, tools and risks, with no sentence saying what matters most.
Opening line: 'The big idea: the company spends more to win customers than it used to, but each one now stays longer, so it still comes out ahead.'
anchors.why: The main point is stated up front and everything else supports it.

criteria.name: Analogies
criteria.fiveMeans: Analogies are apt and not misleading.

anchors.excerpt: 'A data lake is like a swimming pool: people swim in it for fun.'
anchors.why: The analogy is vivid but teaches the wrong thing.

anchors.excerpt: 'A data lake is like a big storage unit where you put boxes in as they are, and sort them only when you need something.'
anchors.why: Maps the key property (store raw now, organize later) onto a familiar thing.
